=========

[![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/sony/gobreaker?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/sony/gobreaker)

[gobreaker][repo-url] implements the [Circuit Breaker pattern](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dn589784.aspx) in Go.

Installation
------------

```
go get github.com/sony/gobreaker
```

Usage
-----

The struct `CircuitBreaker` is a state machine to prevent sending requests that are likely to fail.
The function `NewCircuitBreaker` creates a new `CircuitBreaker`.

```go
func NewCircuitBreaker(st Settings) *CircuitBreaker
```

You can configure `CircuitBreaker` by the struct `Settings`:

```go
type Settings struct {
	Name          string
	MaxRequests   uint32
	Interval      time.Duration
	Timeout       time.Duration
	ReadyToTrip   func(counts Counts) bool
	OnStateChange func(name string, from State, to State)
	IsSuccessful  func(err error) bool
}
```

- `Name` is the name of the `CircuitBreaker`.

- `MaxRequests` is the maximum number of requests allowed to pass through
  when the `CircuitBreaker` is half-open.
  If `MaxRequests` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` allows only 1 request.

- `Interval` is the cyclic period of the closed state
  for `CircuitBreaker` to clear the internal `Counts`, described later in this section.
  If `Interval` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` doesn't clear the internal `Counts` during the closed state.

- `Timeout` is the period of the open state,
  after which the state of `CircuitBreaker` becomes half-open.
  If `Timeout` is 0, the timeout value of `CircuitBreaker` is set to 60 seconds.

- `ReadyToTrip` is called with a copy of `Counts` whenever a request fails in the closed state.
  If `ReadyToTrip` returns true, `CircuitBreaker` will be placed into the open state.
  If `ReadyToTrip` is `nil`, default `ReadyToTrip` is used.
  Default `ReadyToTrip` returns true when the number of consecutive failures is more than 5.

- `OnStateChange` is called whenever the state of `CircuitBreaker` changes.

- `IsSuccessful` is called with the error returned from a request.
  If `IsSuccessful` returns true, the error is counted as a success.
  Otherwise the error is counted as a failure.
  If `IsSuccessful` is nil, default `IsSuccessful` is used, which returns false for all non-nil errors.

The struct `Counts` holds the numbers of requests and their successes/failures:

```go
type Counts struct {
	Requests             uint32
	TotalSuccesses       uint32
	TotalFailures        uint32
	ConsecutiveSuccesses uint32
	ConsecutiveFailures  uint32
}
```

`CircuitBreaker` clears the internal `Counts` either
on the change of the state or at the closed-state intervals.
`Counts` ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing.

`CircuitBreaker` can wrap any function to send a request:

```go
func (cb *CircuitBreaker) Execute(req func() (interface{}, error)) (interface{}, error)
```

The method `Execute` runs the given request if `CircuitBreaker` accepts it.
`Execute` returns an error instantly if `CircuitBreaker` rejects the request.
Otherwise, `Execute` returns the result of the request.
If a panic occurs in the request, `CircuitBreaker` handles it as an error
and causes the same panic again.

Example
-------

```go
var cb *breaker.CircuitBreaker

func Get(url string) ([]byte, error) {
	body, err := cb.Execute(func() (interface{}, error) {
		resp, err := http.Get(url)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		defer resp.Body.Close()
		body, err := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		return body, nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return body.([]byte), nil
}
```

See [example](https://github.com/sony/gobreaker/blob/master/example) for details.

You are an agent in a repository that uses StateRadar. This document tells you what the system is. It shows how information flows through the system. It lists the rules that bind you. The language layer (STE/DTK) is a separate concern.

## 1. What this is

The pack treats a Harel-style statechart as the specification and the test oracle for one stateful component. The division of work does not change. You extract, classify, draft, and propose. Deterministic code verifies your outputs. The human owner decides domain semantics.

Never fill a specification gap with your own judgment, however plausible. Your value is completeness and honesty, not decisiveness.

## 2. The objects

* **Machine boundary**: the scope statement declares one bounded component. The machine boundary is this component, not the whole system.
* **State**: a state is a mode of the component. Implicit states count. Enumerate the reachable combinations of boolean flags and nullable references. These combinations are the real state space.
* **Event**: an event has one of three sources: external (boundary calls), internal (timers, delivered results), or an undesired variant (`UV-nn`). Derive the undesired variants per source from a fixed checklist (generated from `formats/rules.toml`):

<!-- generated:rules key=uv-categories -->
* loss or failure of the source (F-12, sidecar key: `loss`)
* delay beyond timeout (F-13, sidecar key: `delay`)
* duplication (F-14, sidecar key: `duplication`)
* out-of-order or stale arrival, especially after cancellation or shutdown (F-15, sidecar key: `out-of-order`)
* contradictory simultaneous inputs (F-16, sidecar key: `contradiction`)
* spontaneous commission — an event with no legitimate trigger (spurious wakeup, callback without a matching request, unsolicited push) (F-17, sidecar key: `commission`)
* subtle value fault — a plausible but wrong payload (foreign session or entity id, stale epoch or generation counter) (F-18, sidecar key: `value`)
<!-- /generated:rules -->

  The coverage table must show every category. Write a reason for each `n/a`.
* **Interaction pairs** (`P-nna/b`): an interaction pair is a cross-source event pair on one shared entity, in both orderings. Per-source checklists structurally miss races between sources. Interaction pairs close this gap.
* **Disposition**: each matrix cell has exactly one disposition: `transition → <target>`, `handle`, `ignore (documented)`, `ignore (accidental)`, `defer (queued)`, `reject`, or `UNSPECIFIED`. The values `ignore (accidental)` and `UNSPECIFIED` are holes.
* **Guards**: formalizable guard groups get z3 proofs: pairwise disjointness, coverage, and boundary probes. Each group ends as `proven`, `violation`, or `not-formalizable: <reason>`. Never skip a guard group silently.
* **Invariants**: `NAT` marks an assumption about the environment. Cite the assumption into the callee or upstream. `SYS` marks an obligation of the system. Check each SYS invariant state by state.
* **Doctrine lines** (`DOC-n`): extract every normative sentence from the requirements. Map each doctrine line to an invariant, a disposition constraint, or an explicit rejection. An unmapped doctrine line is an error.
* **Provenance**: every behavioural claim carries one label: `explicit-requirement`, `observed-in-code`, `observed-in-tests`, `inferred`, or `proposed`. Code and test citations carry a fragment: `file:line ("fragment")`. The checkers verify the fragment near that line.
* **Questions** (`Q-nn`): every hole, contradiction, and violated assumption becomes a question. Only the human can answer it. Drop nothing in consolidation. Every hole cell carries `→ Q-nn`.
* **Decision records** (`DR-nnn.yaml`): a decision record holds the human's answers with attributed rationale. The decision records are the permanent memory. A to-be deviation without a DR is an error.
* **Sidecar and manifest**: `analysis.json` holds your machine-readable claims. `manifest.json` holds `analyzedSha` and the watch paths. The pack checker consumes both files. Git diffs against the SHA turn staleness into a CI signal.

## 3. The loop

```text
01 Scout      rank stateful components; evidence-based, read-only
02 Pilot      Part A: extract → as-is model → catalogue → matrix → guards
              → invariants → adversarial traces → open questions
              Part B: a BLIND session predicts dispositions from the
              catalogue + requirements only; a diff classifies every row
   (human)    answers the questions — interview mode: one per round,
              recommended option first (Enter default), attributed
              rationale, write-through per answer, defer stays OPEN
03 Resolution DRs, to-be model, matrix update, re-run all checkers
04 Testgen    one test per matrix cell + scenario tests from decided
              traces; red tests against current code = deviation report
              = the implementation worklist, never a test defect
   (impl.)    fix code DR by DR; docs-only DRs first (no red test
              reminds you); tests are read-only
06 Reconcile  after green: promote to-be → as-is, refresh citations at
              HEAD, write sidecar + manifest, archive superseded files
07 Test audit off-cycle: weak tests first (structure over function),
              then redundancy, deviations, gaps; propose, never delete
```

Run 06 first when the manifest reports staleness. Run 01 or 02 for a new component. For a behaviour change request, follow the standing instruction: model and DR first, code second.
## 4. Rules that do not bend

<!-- rule:R-NO-SILENT-DECISIONS -->
1. **Never decide domain semantics.** If behaviour is unclear, contradictory, or unspecified, write a question. Treat a "benign" gap as a proposal inside the question. It is never a reason to omit the question.
<!-- rule:R-REQUIREMENT-SCOPE-a -->
2. **Requirement-scope rule.** A citation covers only the scenario that its text describes. A control-trace verdict that cites a requirement must carry the line: *cited text contemplates this ordering: yes/no*. A "no" voids the verdict. Then raise a question.
<!-- rule:R-SEAM-CONTRACT -->
3. **Read callee contracts. Do not infer them.** Missing error handling at a call site is not evidence that failures propagate. Read the contract of the seam. Cite into the callee.
<!-- rule:R-EXECUTED-CHECKS -->
4. **Run checks as executed code.** You emit data. The pack verifies it with `tools/dsc_check.py` on the sidecar. When you write per-run checkers, run them and paste the output. A red checker means: fix the artefact, or fix the checker openly and re-run. Never "fix" the data to silence a check.
<!-- rule:R-PROPOSALS -->
5. **Proposals are not decisions.** Recommendations have flipped between runs on the same code. Present them, label them `proposed`, and hold them loosely. Pre-selection in the interview is presentation, not authority.
<!-- rule:R-ANTI-MIRRORING -->
6. **Tests bind to behaviour, not structure.** Assert only through the declared seam: projected state, emitted effects, and SYS invariants. Never weaken, skip, or delete a test to make it pass. A failing cell test is a finding.
<!-- rule:R-PART-B -->
7. **Part B stays blind.** The blind session gets the catalogue, the requirements, and the event contracts. It never gets the code, the matrix, or prior analyses. Do no git archaeology on deleted analyses.
<!-- rule:R-DEFERRED-OPEN -->
8. **Deferred stays OPEN.** A deferred question blocks only its own cells.
<!-- rule:R-READ-PROMPTS -->
9. **Read prompts in full.** When a task says "run prompt X" or references a prompt file (e.g. `prompts/02-pilot.md`), read the complete file before producing output. Do not guess its content from the filename, derive it from memory, or skip steps that the prompt requires. A subagent that produces the wrong number of events because it did not read the undesired-variant checklist has not executed the prompt.

## 5. What the checkers catch

The checkers catch the following defects. Do not fight them. (Generated from `formats/rules.toml` — the registry maps each line to its rule, checker, and selftest.)

<!-- generated:rules key=checker-catalogue -->
* grid totality
* disposition vocabulary
* hole → Q back-references
* DR links on ignore, reject, and defer
* behavioural-DR reverse coverage: every decided change connects to a cell
* pair → trace coverage
* guard outcomes present
* coverage-table totality
* Mermaid ↔ matrix sync
* fragment citations within ±3 lines
* manifest staleness
* blind-table row coverage
* schema validity of the sidecar
* existence of every cited DR file
* reachable states and terminal-state marking
* state names follow PA-17 (PascalCase segments or ALL-CAPS API enums)
* doctrine-line mapping totality (DOC-n → cell / invariant / rejected)
* event classification present per catalogue event (PA-4)
* abstraction statement in the matrix (PA-10)
* scope lines on citing control traces
* gate-type annotation presence on events
* opt-in cell rationale completeness and source-backed scope
* upstream-guard annotation presence on events
<!-- /generated:rules -->

## 6. Failure modes seen in real runs

Avoid these failure modes from real runs.

* Call-site inference declared a publisher failure path. The callee's contract excludes this path.
* An agent applied a recorded decision for steady state to a race. The decision never contemplated this race.
* A checklist category silently produced no variant.
* A catalogue stated gates but not remembrance semantics. Remembrance semantics say what ended entities leave behind. Blind readers misread five rows for that one omission.
* Consolidation lost findings between runs.
* An agent almost softened an expected-red test instead of reporting it.

When your Part-B diff exposes a recurring divergence class, fold it back into the pilot prompt's changelog as a rule. Single findings stay findings. The goal is not zero divergence. A blind pass that cannot disagree is dead weight.

- **Completion-report drift.** Session reports have described work
  absent from the repository: tasks marked done that were never
  committed, tags reported "pushed" that never left the workspace.

- **Hollow checks.** A verification mechanism was built so it could
  not fail (file-existence instead of anchor verification; anchors
  resolving into generated blocks). The countermeasure is R-RED-PROBE:

- **Vacuous green.** A relocated test runner reported "0/0 cases

- **First-contact failures.** Across one extended session, every tool
  change shipped without a simultaneous gate arrived defective but

## 7. Working on this pack

The rules above govern the analysis. These govern changes to the pack

in real pack-development sessions.

1. **Completion = diff + executed acceptance.** Describe only work

{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "# Local model routing

The implemented commands support bounded drafting, a draft-and-verify chain,
batched semantic checks and offline evaluation. They do not automatically
accept a draft or route difficult cases to a stronger model. The next pilot
and its evaluation criteria are in the [model cascade
plan](plan-model-cascade.md); broader project work is in the
[roadmap](roadmap.md).

This optional workflow sends supplied text to DeepSeek and TypeSafe. Set
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment. Each pilot uses
a separate SQLite ledger stored outside the repository. The default ledger
limit is $2, expressed as 2,000,000 microdollars.

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/state/stateradar"
ledger="$HOME/.local/state/stateradar/example-pilot.sqlite"
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" status
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" flash /path/to/task-and-source.txt
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" jev /path/to/source.txt \
  'Does the source explicitly describe the specified event ordering?' --model jev-1.14.0
```

A new ledger takes its limit from `--limit-microdollars` on the first call
(default 2,000,000). The flag only sets the initial limit: passing a different
value to an existing ledger fails, so change it with `set-limit`.

The Flash input must include the task and the source excerpts needed to do it.
Each invocation is a fresh text-only call. Flash cannot browse the repo or
execute tools through this interface. A calling agent prepares inputs, checks
citations and results, runs the deterministic checkers, and carries forward
every uncertainty and question. Jev returns a probability; it does not
establish a domain decision.

### Batch semantic checks

Use `jev-batch` to evaluate independent claims and event orderings against the
same source file in one request. Supply a JSON array such as:

```json
[
  {"id": "C1", "kind": "claim", "statement": "The component stays failed.", "line": 12, "fragment": "remains in FAILED"},
  {"id": "O1", "kind": "ordering", "statement": "A disconnect occurs after failure.", "line": 12, "fragment": "remains in FAILED"}
]
```

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" jev-batch \
  /path/to/source.md /path/to/checks.json --model jev-1.14.0 --output /path/to/batch.json
```

For shorter tool results, add `--summary` with `--output`. Stdout carries
the artifact path, usage, and counts by choice. The output file keeps every
judgment and its citation. For `flash`, use `--output draft.json` to save
the draft and print usage. If Flash truncates the draft, the command exits
with an error and keeps it at `draft.json.partial.json`.

Each `line` is a one-based integer line in the source file. Each `fragment` is
a single line of at least four non-space characters that occurs on a line
within three lines of it, the pack-wide citation window. The `draft-verify`
prompt asks Flash for the cited line itself; the check accepts the window.
Missing fragments, invalid lines, duplicate IDs and incomplete responses fail.
All questions see the same source and are evaluated independently. Prepare a
separate batch for another source. The response includes the source path and
content hash, citation, statement, model version, choice probabilities, token
usage, and cost. Every result is marked for review. Ordering checks also
receive an independently evaluated `ordering_scope_probability` for whether
the fragment establishes every material condition, actor, event, order and
outcome in the asserted sequence. Paraphrases count when they preserve the
meaning. Surrounding text cannot supply missing evidence. The Choice and
Noul answers may disagree; preserve both and examine the source. Confidence
and repeatability do not establish correctness. Follow the requirement-scope rule and raise a
question when its conditions require one. An API error after reservation keeps
the reservation until reconciled. Omit `--model` to use `jev-latest`; pin a
specific available version for comparable measurements.

### Draft and verify

`draft-verify` chains the two models for one source file. Flash receives the
task and the numbered source and must answer with JSON: a `claims` list (`id`,
`kind` = `claim` or `ordering`, `statement`, `line`, `fragment`) and a
`questions` list. Code rejects a draft that is not this structure, and a draft
cut off at the output budget (`finish_reason=length`); either way the raw text
is saved next to the output with the extension replaced (`--output
review.json` gives `review.draft.txt`) and is not printed. The default output
budget is 12000 tokens: 4096 truncated a 248-line source, whose complete draft
then took about 5,200, so 12000 leaves headroom (the ledger reserves 1.2 times
the budget for output). Each claim's citation is then checked against the
source with the same rule as `jev-batch`. Claims that fail keep their reason
in `citation_check` and are never sent to Jev. The citable claims go to Jev in
one batch.

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" draft-verify \
  docs/requirements.md /path/to/task.md --output /path/to/draft-review.json \
  --model jev-1.14.0
```

The result records the source path and hash, the Flash and Jev usage, every
claim with its citation check and Jev judgment, and every draft question. The
command prints a summary (counts, citation failures, Jev choices, usage); the
full result is only in the output file. If Jev fails after the draft was paid
for, the result is still written, with the error in `verification.error` and
no Jev judgments, and the command exits 1. Everything is marked for review;
nothing is accepted. `prompts/02-pilot.md` ("Model routing") says which pilot
steps use this command and how the calling agent consolidates the result,
including the rule that an ordering counts as source-backed only when Jev's
choice is `supported` and its scope probability is at least 0.5. That cut-off
is provisional and uncalibrated: it can only turn an ordering into a question
and never accepts one. The command needs both API keys. Every command that
takes `--output` checks before any request that the output is not a directory
and its directory is writable.

### Draft matrix cells

`draft-cells` drafts disposition-matrix cells (the 02-pilot routing variant
`flash-writes`, roadmap entry 11 item 2). The task file is JSON written by the
steering agent: `states` (each a `name` and the `condition` that defines it),
`events` (each an `id` and a `gist`) and optional `notes`; names and ids are
one word, and rule 10 of the routing section (finding-neutral tasks) applies
to all of it. Flash must answer with one cell per state and event (`state`,
`event`, `disposition`, `target` for a transition, `line`, `fragment`, `note`)
plus `questions`. Code checks each cell: known state and event, the closed
disposition vocabulary of `formats/rules.toml`, a transition target among the
states, no target on other dispositions, the citation rule of `jev-batch`, and
one cell per pair; it lists the pairs without a cell. Every matrix tool splits
table rows on `|`, so a fragment with a `|` is cut to its longest verbatim
piece without one (refused if that piece is too short) and a note's `|`
becomes `/`. Every clean cell goes to one Jev batch as a claim that names the
state with its condition, the event with its gist and the drafted outcome. The
default output budget is 16384 tokens, the Flash maximum; split the events
across task files when a draft is cut off.

The result JSON holds every cell with its problems and Jev judgment, the
missing pairs, the draft questions and the usage. The command also writes a
matrix block next to the JSON (`cells.json` gives `cells.md`): the 02-pilot
cell form in sub-tables of eight events, then a review list (cells with
problems, cells Jev did not judge `supported`, missing pairs) and the draft
questions. A hole or a cell with a problem carries `→ Q-?` (a cell with a
problem also loses its citation), and a missing cell reads `MISSING`, so
`dsc_check.py` fails until the agent has decided each. Nothing is accepted:
the agent checks every cell against the source. A draft that is not the
required JSON, or is cut off, is kept as `cells.draft.txt`. The command needs
both API keys.

`python3 tools/draft_cells.py compare cells.json … --sidecar analysis.json`
needs no key: it compares the drafts with the run's final sidecar and counts
each drafted cell as unchanged, changed (disposition, target or citation) or
dropped, split by Jev's choice, and lists the final cells no draft held.
Add `--output compare.json` to keep all rows in the report file and print
aggregate counts.

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" draft-cells \
  pool/channel.go /path/to/cells-task.json --output /path/to/cells.json \
  --model jev-1.14.0
```

## Pilot runner output

`tools/run_sol_pilot.py` runs the pilot on macOS through the signed-in Codex
CLI. It requires the two routing provider keys and a local clone of the
pinned Pool or gobreaker source. It defaults to one analysis with selective
output.

```bash

  --output /tmp/stateradar-pool-run
```
Ordinary output up to 12,000 characters per stream is returned in full.
For longer documents, follow the supplied
`read_more.next_stdout` or `read_more.next_stderr` command and then each
returned `next` to read contiguous pages. Long Go test timeout and race
reports show the relevant stacks and their positions in the full log.
Both streams are retained for every command.

For targeted evidence, use the command tool with
`["read-log", "012", "function", "Put"]`,
`["read-log", "012", "rows", "GetAgain"]`,
`["read-log", "012", "lines", "20", "45"]`, or
`["read-log", "012", "find", "generation"]`.

`line_counts` for the retained streams. A line range may end beyond EOF and
returns the available lines; its start must exist and its requested width
must not exceed 100 lines. A range starting at line 1 of an empty stream
returns an empty result with `total_lines: 0`. The response includes the actual
total line count. The canonical routing command also accepts `--help` without
making a provider call or creating a ledger.

Use `--output-mode standard` or `--output-mode compact` for one run in
the corresponding comparison format. Use `--output-mode compare` for
the standard/compact pair. `--compact-first` can be used alone as
shorthand for the pair in reverse order.

## Structured matrix and hybrid pilots

Use `--routing-variant routed` for standard routing. The `matrix` variant
keeps that routing and adds the structured matrix workflow and its two
postflight gates. The `hybrid` variant additionally asks Flash for concurrent
schedules. All three use the same selective output by default.

Use `--routing-variant hybrid` with the Codex runner. Flash proposes
bounded concurrent schedules against one implementation file per call.
Every candidate includes cited ordered steps and observable outcomes.
The tool marks fragment or shape problems, and the pilot reviews every
candidate against the source before using it. For example:

```sh
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger /tmp/pilot.sqlite flash-windows \
  /path/to/component.go --output /tmp/windows.json
```

The full run retains the raw provider answer and the candidate review.
In both `matrix` and `hybrid`, Codex writes the matrix fields and uses `tools/hybrid_pilot.py` to render
them. The renderer checks totality, vocabulary, question IDs, source
fragments and round trips through the sidecar parser. The runner checks
matrix identity and regenerates the sidecar before running the five pack
gates. Jev continues to verify cited claims and requirement scope.

## Provider limits (checked 2026-11-12)

From the TypeSafe and DeepSeek documentation:

* Jev accepts at most 64k tokens per request (source plus all questions) and
  32k per question (source plus one question). A larger request fails with
  HTTP 400 `max_tokens_exceeded`; split the source into excerpts instead of
  enabling the slower long-context mode. English is Jev's primary language;
  checks over other languages are less accurate.
* `jev-latest` and `jev-preview` currently resolve to `jev-1.14.0`. Aliases
  move with releases, so pin the versioned ID for comparable measurements.
  The response's `model` field records the version that answered.
* There is no batch endpoint: `jev-batch` sends all questions for one source
  in one request. TypeSafe's parallel-questions cookbook reports the same
  answers as separate calls at a fraction of the input cost; this is not
  measured for StateRadar.
* `deepseek-flash` is the current Flash model name; DeepSeek serves it as
  DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. Off-peak rates are half the peak rates used for
  the reservation below.
* Both clients retry HTTP 429, 503 and 529 up to three times, with a
  120-second timeout per attempt. A numeric `Retry-After` is honoured up to
  60 seconds; an absent, non-finite or HTTP-date value falls back to
  exponential backoff (1, 2, 4 s). Other errors fail at once. A retried
  request stays within the same ledger reservation.
* The cookbook thresholds (for example 0.7 in the SDE cascade, 0.8 for
  citation auto-acceptance) are calibrated on the vendor's data. They are not
  StateRadar acceptance rules; see the [cascade plan](plan-model-cascade.md).

## Accounting and recovery

The tool reserves an estimated maximum before each request using byte length,
the requested output limit, and peak published prices. It records usage after
a response. Flash input is charged at the peak cache-miss rate in this
estimate even when the provider reports a cache hit. Jev output is free at the
current listed price. Rates are $0.30 per million Flash input tokens, $1.20
per million Flash output tokens, and $0.042 per million Jev input tokens.
Update the implementation when provider prices change.

The reservation is an estimate, not a provider-enforced spending cap. If
actual usage exceeds it, the ledger records the actual amount and blocks
future calls when the limit is exceeded. Timeouts, invalid usage responses,
and interrupted calls retain their reservations, since their actual costs are
unknown. Concurrent calls to one ledger reserve using SQLite transactions. The
ledger covers only calls through these tools. The main agent or any other
provider has separate billing, so any budget for strong-model review is not
enforced here. Failed requests and provider billing changes may also make the
ledger differ from an invoice.

A failed request reports its reservation id, and for an HTTP error the start
of the provider's error body (for example `max_tokens_exceeded`). If the
provider answered but the ledger could not record it (a locked database), the
answer is printed (in `draft-verify`, kept as
`verification.unrecorded_response` with a `question_claims` map to claim ids)
and the error names the exact `settle` command. If Jev answers but the answer
fails validation, `draft-verify` records its settled tokens and cost next to
the error. Inspect reservations with `status`. After checking the provider's
usage, reconcile an uncertain call with `settle CALL_ID ACTUAL_MICRODOLLARS`.
Change the limit deliberately with `set-limit MICRODOLLARS`.

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" status
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" settle 1 1200
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" set-limit 3000000
```

The ledger includes no prompt text, but its database is local task data.

The pilot runner defaults to `--routing-variant routed` with selective

that the catalogue still matches those fields. Coverage omissions,
unknown UV references, and inconsistent UV prefixes fail before writing.
`pilot_artifacts.py citations SOURCE LINE [LINE ...]` copies exact source
lines as JSON without judging the associated claim.

Blind coverage accepts distinct situations for the same event, with an
explicit Situation column; duplicate or missing situation labels fail.
The checklist still ticks each event and pair ordering exactly once.
A Part-A controller never edits a blind response to make it pass.

The controller runs with `--sandbox workspace-write` in the disposable
component checkout, matching its artifact-writing task. The pilot command
server still applies its macOS sandbox and restricts credentials to routing

### Usage checkpoints and interrupted pilots

The runner now keeps its fresh Codex session on disk rather than using
`--ephemeral`. Authentication still uses the existing ChatGPT login and
`--ignore-user-config`. Prompts and tool transcripts therefore also remain in
Codex's local session storage. The supervisor reads only the rollout whose ID
was emitted by its own child; it does not inspect unrelated chat contents.

`usage-history.jsonl` records changed cumulative counters from local

"""Guard-proof procedures for disposition-matrix guard groups (z3).

The pack's method requires, per guard group (PA-1/PA-2, 02-pilot
step 4): pairwise disjointness, coverage (or an explicit else), and
boundary probes for every comparison. Per-run `check_guards.py`
scripts used to reimplement this z3 boilerplate per component — the
same duplication check_matrix.py ended for the matrix checks (v1.23).

This module is the shared procedure. A per-run script contributes only
the component-specific part: typed z3 variables, NAT-domain
assumptions, and the guard expressions. It must never reimplement the
proof loop.

    import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "<pack>/tools")
    import guard_proofs, z3

    retry = z3.Int("retryCount")
    nat = [retry >= 0, retry <= 5]                       # NAT domain
    res = guard_proofs.check_group(
        "reconnect-decision",
        [("retry", retry < 5), ("give-up", retry >= 5)],
        assumptions=nat)
    print(guard_proofs.render([res]))                    # guard-results.txt

Dependencies: tools/requirements-dev.txt (z3-solver). A guard that
cannot be formalized never reaches this module — it gets the
`not-formalizable: <category>` mark instead (PA-3b).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class GroupResult:
    name: str
    outcome: str                      # "proven" | "violation"
    findings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def _z3():
    try:
        import z3
        return z3
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(
            "guard_proofs needs z3-solver — install the dev dependencies: "
            "pip install -r tools/requirements-dev.txt "
            "(or: uv run --with-requirements tools/requirements-dev.txt ...)"
        ) from exc


def _witness(model, decls_of_interest) -> str:
    parts = []
    for d in model.decls():
        if not decls_of_interest or d.name() in decls_of_interest:
            parts.append(f"{d.name()}={model[d]}")
    return ", ".join(sorted(parts)) or "<any assignment>"


def check_group(name: str, guards, assumptions=(), has_else: bool = False) -> GroupResult:
    """Prove PA-1 (pairwise disjointness) and PA-2 (coverage) for one
    guard group under the declared NAT assumptions.

    guards: list of (label, z3.BoolRef) pairs.
    assumptions: iterable of z3.BoolRef (the NAT domain).
    has_else: True when the code has an explicit else branch — coverage
    is then discharged by construction and only disjointness is proven.
    """
    z3 = _z3()
    findings: list[str] = []

    # PA-1: every pair unsatisfiable together
    for i in range(len(guards)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(guards)):
            (la, ga), (lb, gb) = guards[i], guards[j]
            s = z3.Solver()
            s.add(*assumptions)
            s.add(ga, gb)
            if s.check() == z3.sat:
                findings.append(
                    f"PA-1 overlap: {la!r} and {lb!r} both fire "
                    f"(witness: {_witness(s.model(), None)}) — order decides")

    # PA-2: the disjunction covers the domain, or an explicit else exists
    if not has_else:
        s = z3.Solver()
        s.add(*assumptions)
        s.add(z3.Not(z3.Or(*[g for _, g in guards])))
        if s.check() == z3.sat:
            findings.append(
                f"PA-2 gap: no guard fires "
                f"(witness: {_witness(s.model(), None)}) — hole, or add an "
                f"explicit else and pass has_else=True with a citation")

    return GroupResult(name=name,
                       outcome="violation" if findings else "proven",
                       findings=findings)


def boundary_probe(guards, assignments) -> list[tuple[dict, list[str]]]:
    """Evaluate which guard labels fire for concrete assignments —
    below, exactly at, and above every comparison limit (02-pilot
    step 4c). assignments: list of {z3-const: python value} dicts.
    Returns [(assignment, [labels that fire]), ...] for the report.
    """
    z3 = _z3()

    def lift(v):
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            return z3.BoolVal(v)
        if isinstance(v, int):
            return z3.IntVal(v)
        if isinstance(v, float):
            return z3.RealVal(v)
        return v  # already a z3 expr

    rows = []
    for a in assignments:
        subs = [(var, lift(val)) for var, val in a.items()]
        labels = [label for label, g in guards
                  if z3.is_true(z3.simplify(z3.substitute(g, *subs)))]
        rows.append(({str(k): v for k, v in a.items()}, labels))
    return rows


def render(results) -> str:
    """guard-results.txt format: one outcome line per group, findings
    indented. not-formalizable groups are appended by the per-run
    script itself (they never reach z3)."""
    lines = []
    for r in results:
        lines.append(f"group {r.name}: {r.outcome}")

"""Generic per-component matrix checker (the 02-pilot stage-1/stage-2 check).

Every pilot I ran duplicated this logic per component (dobby session,
2026-08-05: four near-identical scripts). This is the shared version:
it parses the machine-readable declarations (never prose) and checks
grid coverage, citation presence, hole→Q links, and pair→trace links.

Checks:
- Stage 1: every row covers every catalogue event exactly once (rows
  accumulate across sub-tables); every reject / ignore (documented) /
  defer cell carries a citation (`file.py:NNN`, a DR id, or an explicit
  `inferred` marker); no empty cells.
- Stage 2: every hole cell (UNSPECIFIED / ignore (accidental)) carries
  a `→ Q-nn` reference that exists in open-questions.md; every
  interaction pair id in the catalogue appears in adversarial-traces.md.

Usage: python3 tools/check_matrix.py <analysis-dir>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# A citation is `file.<ext>:NNN` in any implementation language (the
# pack claims language neutrality; ".py:" alone silently failed every
# Go/TS/Rust matrix — grpc-go addrconn pilot, 2026-08-07), a DR id, or
# an explicit `inferred` marker.
CITATION_OK = ("DR-", "inferred")
CITATION_RE = re.compile(r"[\w./-]+\.[A-Za-z]{1,4}:\d+")


def _events(catalogue: str) -> list[str]:
    m = re.search(r"<!-- event-ids: (.+?) -->", catalogue)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError("catalogue: no event-ids declaration comment")
    return m.group(1).split()


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    adir = Path(sys.argv[1])
    errors: list[str] = []

    cat_path = adir / "event-catalogue.md"
    if not cat_path.is_file():
        print(f"CHECK MATRIX: no event-catalogue.md in {adir}")
        return 2
    cat = cat_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    events = _events(cat)

    matrix = (adir / "disposition-matrix.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "<!-- states:" not in matrix:
        errors.append("matrix: no states declaration comment")

    # PA-17 state naming: PascalCase segments joined by "_"
    # (Open_AwaitingStability), ALL-CAPS API enums (CONNECTING,
    # TRANSIENT_FAILURE), compound row labels word by word ("Open Idle").
    # A name a blind reader cannot derive — implementation flags,
    # comparisons, lowercase — is a modelling error.
    word_ok = re.compile(r"^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$")
    names: list[str] = []
    decl = re.search(r"<!-- states: (.+?) -->", matrix)
    if decl:
        raw = decl.group(1)
        names = ([s.strip() for s in raw.split(",")] if "," in raw
                 else raw.split())
        for name in names:
            for word in name.split(" "):
                if word and not word_ok.match(word):
                    errors.append(
                        f"state {name!r} violates PA-17 naming "
                        f"(offending word {word!r}: use PascalCase segments "
                        f"with '_' separators or the ALL-CAPS API enum name)")

    rows: dict[str, int] = {}
    for line in matrix.split("\n"):
        s = line.strip()
        if not s.startswith("| **"):
            continue
        label = s.split("|")[1].strip().replace("**", "").strip()
        cells = s.split("|")[2:-1]
        rows[label] = rows.get(label, 0) + len(cells)
        for cell in cells:
            c = cell.strip()
            if not c:
                errors.append(f"empty cell in row {label}")
                continue
            if (
                c.startswith(("reject", "ignore (documented", "defer"))
                and not CITATION_RE.search(c)
                and not any(tok in c for tok in CITATION_OK)
                and "Q-" not in c
            ):
                errors.append(f"uncited {c[:50]!r} in row {label}")

    terminal_match = re.search(r"<!-- terminal: (.+?) -->", matrix)
    terminal = set(re.split(r"[,\s]+", terminal_match.group(1))) if terminal_match else set()
    for name in names:
        if name not in rows and name not in terminal:
            errors.append(f"missing state row: {name}")
    for name, count in rows.items():
        if name not in names:
            errors.append(f"undeclared state row: {name}")
        if count != len(events):
            errors.append(f"grid row {name}: {count} cells, expected {len(events)}")

    total = sum(rows.values())
    if total != len(events) * len(rows):
        errors.append(
            f"grid: {total} cells across {len(rows)} rows, "
            f"expected {len(events)} per row"
        )

    # Stage 1: undesired-coverage totality, when the catalogue carries
    # the table (an empty cell is an error — a checklist category must
    # never silently produce no variant).
    if "## Undesired-coverage" in cat:
        cov = cat.split("## Undesired-coverage")[1].split("##")[0]
        for line in cov.split("\n"):
            if (
                line.strip().startswith("|")
                and "**" not in line
                and "---" not in line
                and "source" not in line.lower()
            ):
                cells = [c.strip() for c in line.split("|")[1:-1]]
                for c in cells[1:]:
                    if not c:
                        errors.append(f"coverage: empty cell in {cells[0]}")

    # Stage 2: hole cells carry Q refs present in open-questions.md
    oq_path = adir / "open-questions.md"
    oq = oq_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if oq_path.is_file() else ""
    qids = set(re.findall(r"\b(Q-[\w-]+)\b", oq))
    for m in re.finditer(r"(UNSPECIFIED|ignore \(accidental\))[^\n|]*", matrix):
        q = re.search(r"Q-[\w-]+", m.group(0))
        if not q:
            errors.append(f"hole cell without Q ref: {m.group(0)[:60]!r}")
        elif q.group(0) not in qids:
            errors.append(f"hole cell: {q.group(0)} not in open-questions.md")

    # PA-10: completeness is relative to a declared abstraction —
    # the matrix must state it (a line starting "Abstraction").
    if not re.search(r"^Abstraction", matrix, re.M):
        errors.append(
            "matrix: no abstraction statement (PA-10) — add a line "
            "starting 'Abstraction' declaring what completeness is "
            "relative to (hierarchy inheritance, guard predicates)")

    # PA-4: every catalogue event carries an external/internal
    # classification in the events table. An undesired variant may
    # inherit it by referencing a classified base event in its row
    # (the UV table's base/source column).
    cat_rows = [ln.strip() for ln in cat.split("\n")
                if ln.strip().startswith("|")]

    def rows_for(ev: str) -> list[str]:
        return [r for r in cat_rows
                if re.match(rf"\|\s*\*{{0,2}}{re.escape(ev)}(?![\w-])", r)]

    classified = {ev for ev in events
                  if any(re.search(r"\b(external|internal)\b", r)
                         for r in rows_for(ev))}
    for ev in events:
        if ev in classified:
            continue
        inherits = any(
            re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){re.escape(base)}(?![\w-])", r)
            for r in rows_for(ev) for base in classified)
        if not inherits:
            errors.append(
                f"event {ev}: no external/internal classification in the "
                f"catalogue table, and no classified base event referenced "
                f"(PA-4)")

    # Stage 2: every pair id appears in the traces; control-trace
    # verdicts that cite a requirement or decision carry the scope
    # line (requirement-scope rule): "cited text contemplates this
    # ordering: yes/no". Blocks are split on trace headers, bold or
    # markdown headings ('**T-01', '### T-01'); a file with no recognised
    # header would be one block and pass vacuously.
    traces_path = adir / "adversarial-traces.md"
    if traces_path.is_file():
        traces = traces_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for pair in sorted(set(re.findall(r"P-\d+[ab]", cat))):
            if pair not in traces:
                errors.append(f"pair {pair} missing from adversarial-traces.md")
        blocks = re.split(r"\n(?=(?:#{1,6}\s+|\*\*)\s*[PTM]-[A-Z]*\d)", traces)
        for block in blocks:
            header = block.split("\n", 1)[0][:40]
            flat = " ".join(block.split())  # scope lines wrap across lines
            if "control trace" not in flat:
                continue
            if not re.search(r"\b(DOC-\d|DR-\d)", flat):
                continue
            if "contemplates this ordering" not in flat:
                errors.append(
                    f"control trace {header!r} cites a requirement/decision "
                    f"but carries no 'cited text contemplates this "
                    f"ordering: yes/no' scope line")

    if errors:
        print("CHECK MATRIX: FAIL")
        for e in errors:
            print(" -", e)
        return 1
    print(f"CHECK MATRIX: OK ({len(rows)} rows x {len(events)} events)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

item.text: The probes reproduced both callback reentry stalls, a duplicate completion closing HalfOpen early, and a stale completion advancing expired Open without updating counters. The probe-only race run passed. The full race run failed on an upstream test that reads counters directly while another goroutine writes them.

`go test -timeout 15s -count=1 -overlay domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/_probe/overlay.json -run '^TestPilot' -v .` passed all ten probes (log 086). The file under _probe is isolated from recursive upstream discovery. The JSON overlay maps an added virtual test file into the package.

- DuplicateDone confirms early closure on a second callback invocation.
- AbandonAndLateReport confirms repeated refusal, then separate late success and failure branches.
- AdmissionOrdering confirms refusal before the closing report and admission after it, supporting P-03a/b.
- ExecuteOvertakes proves result reordering and a new call after retaining the earlier value.
- ExpiryAndStaleReport observes no idle or Counts notification, then stale callback promotion for both Boolean values.
- StaleClassifierAndReturn stages stale accounting with a channel and verifies original error return.
- CallbackReentry measures no return for 25 ms after entering each callback; the sync.Mutex contract establishes the deadlock mechanism. The intentionally blocked goroutines last only until test-process exit.
- CallbackPanics shows double failure accounting, hook commit survival, and replacement of the request panic.
- Goexit shows an admission without outcome.
- SharedRecoveryWaves generates three four-request failure waves.

`go test -race -timeout 20s -overlay domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/_probe/overlay.json -run '^TestPilot' .` passed (log 095). The full overlay run `go test -race -timeout 30s -overlay domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/_probe/overlay.json ./...` failed (log 091). Upstream TestCustomCircuitBreaker reads its internal Counts directly at gobreaker_test.go:258 ("assert.Equal(t, Counts{3, 2, 0, 2, 0}, customCB.counts)") while succeedLater writes through gobreaker.go:56 ("c.Requests++") and gobreaker.go:289 ("cb.counts.onRequest()") under gobreaker.go:277 ("cb.mutex.Lock()"). The test's sleep provides no synchronization. This is evidence of a test-harness race. The public Counts getter locks at gobreaker.go:217 ("cb.mutex.Lock()").

- NAT-02. Every admitted two-step request reports once and truthfully for its own work, and callbacks return normally and promptly. Proposed operating assumptions from the separate report contract at gobreaker.go:262-264 and callback settings at README.md:53-63. Neither delivery nor exactly-once is guaranteed there. Q-01–Q-04, Q-07, Q-13.
- NAT-03. Typed counter and duration domains in check_guards.py. No full-generation wrap assumed for stale-result isolation. The unsigned counters and epoch are observed-in-code gobreaker.go:48 ("Requests             uint32") and gobreaker.go:128 ("generation uint64"). Limits Q-12.

## Q-01

**Question:** May OnStateChange call State, Counts, Execute or Allow on the same breaker, and how should competing callers behave during notification?

**Current behaviour:** The state and generation are committed before the hook. The hook runs under the mutex. A reentrant locking call cannot acquire it and the outer call cannot release it until notification returns. One constructed CircuitBreaker, projected through Execute or its separately constructed TwoStepCircuitBreaker wrapper. Its mutex, counts, generation, time-based admission and synchronous callbacks are inside the boundary. Actors are request callers, outcome reporters, state/count/name readers, the Go runtime clock and synchronization contracts, and the injected work, classification, trip and notification functions. The example's HTTP, response body ownership, caller cancellation and process shutdown live outside the breaker. No neighboring modeled component appears in this checkout. The HTTP seam's owning code is example/http_breaker.go:27-39 and is not a breaker transition.

item.text:
Completed the CircuitBreaker pilot with **22 open domain questions**. The model covers 3 states, 35 events, 105 matrix cells, and 30 representative interaction orderings. The blind pass produced 126 situations, including 19 divergences linked to open questions. [Summary](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-routed/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/summary.md) · [Open questions](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-routed/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/open-questions.md)

- `OnStateChange` and `ReadyToTrip` can deadlock when they re-enter a method that takes the same breaker mutex.
- Calling one two-step completion callback twice can close HalfOpen after only one admitted trial. An abandoned trial can leave a saturated HalfOpen breaker refusing further requests indefinitely.
- A stale completion can advance an expired Open breaker to HalfOpen before its accounting is discarded. `Counts()` alone leaves expiry unobserved.
- A callback panic can replace the original request panic. A panicking trip policy can also cause a failure to be counted twice. [Traces](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-routed/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/adversarial-traces.md)

The catalogue, matrix, strict sidecar, reachability, blind coverage, and artifact audit passed. Z3 proved 17 guard groups. Three groups involving clock or callback behavior were reviewed by inspection. The baseline suite and all ten overlay probes passed, including the probe-only race run. The full race run failed on an unsynchronized counter read in the existing `TestCustomCircuitBreaker`. [Validation](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-routed/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/as-is-validation.md)

Flash and Jev completed with no provider failures. The run records the corrected citation rejection and an ordering assertion that supplied the function after acceptance. Source, existing tests, and configuration were untouched.
